subject: Follow-up: Model fit eval + parity thresholds (PayGrid)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@paygrid.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Model fit eval + parity thresholds (PayGrid)

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and helpful context on PayGrid's prioritization (invoice parsing + entity normalization, high accuracy on vendor/amount extraction, and a handful of high-value error cases). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap
- Scope: model fit for extraction/normalization on PayGrid sample corpus (100k rows anonymized).
- Success metrics discussed: extraction F1 (vendor/name), normalized amount accuracy, end-to-end latency p95 on typical payloads.
- Parity ask: PayGrid asked whether open models can reach parity with your proprietary baseline.

Redwood recommended baseline for the eval
- Proprietary baseline (what you compared to): rwx-3b-prop (our in-house tuned baseline)
- Open candidates we recommend running: open-2.7b-quant, open-7b-llama-compat (quantized), and open-NEOX-3B-opt.

What we propose
1) 7-day model fit eval in our sandbox using your sample dataset. We will run rwx-3b-prop and the three open candidates above.
2) Evaluation artifacts we'll produce: per-prompt-set accuracy breakdowns, confusion matrices, latency percentiles, and an "acceptance matrix" that shows where each model meets/fails your thresholds.
3) Acceptance criteria (please confirm): parity if open model drop <= 2.0% absolute F1 vs proprietary baseline AND latency within 25% of baseline p95.

Attachments
- paygrid_prompt_set_v1.txt (attached) — the initial prompt set we used in the call for parity checks.

Next steps / asks
- Please confirm you approve the 7-day eval and the acceptance thresholds above (F1 delta <= 2.0% & latency within 25%).
- If agreed, can you provide a shared S3 link or upload to the Drive folder we discussed (I've linked it below)? We'll provision a sandbox and share credentials & the eval plan.

Links
- Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PayGridEval

I'll follow up internally to kick off infra and assign owners.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@paygrid.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit eval + parity thresholds (PayGrid)

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear recap. We're aligned on scope and the list of candidate models. A couple quick responses: 

- We approve the 7-day eval.
- Parity threshold: our ideal is <=1.5% absolute F1 drop, but we can accept up to 2.0% if latency remains close to baseline. Please call out where trade-offs are (e.g., model X has slightly lower F1 but much better inference cost).
- I'll share the S3 link and a small anonymized sample CSV by EOD. Tom will be our internal technical contact for dataset/ingest.

Also please include an estimated cost range for the eval (GPU hours + data transfer) so our procurement folks have a ballpark.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Liu
Director, Data Science | PayGrid
sarah.liu@paygrid.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: PayGrid eval kickoff + parity acceptance planning (PG-3421)

Team — moving this internal thread to assign owners and call out known risks. Quick summary: PayGrid approved the 7-day eval and confirmed they'd prefer <=1.5% F1 drop ideally, will accept 2.0% if latency/cost tradeoffs are documented.

Tasks / owners
- Marissa: orchestrate the eval runs (baseline + open candidates), produce the per-prompt-set metrics and the acceptance matrix. Attach eval template (I've stubbed eval_results_baseline_vs_open.csv).
- Aditya: provision sandbox infra, estimate GPU hours + cost, and provide credentials for PayGrid upload.
- Jonas: validate quantization profiles for open models (want to avoid a quality regression from aggressive 4-bit quant).

Quality regression concerns
- We need to capture qualitative failure modes (vendor name truncation, multi-entity grouping errors) in addition to scalar F1 numbers. Add a short "failure case" doc for PayGrid ops to review.

Acceptance thresholds (proposal for internal alignment)
- Strict: delta_F1 <= 1.5% AND p95_latency <= 1.2x baseline
- Soft: delta_F1 <= 2.0% AND p95_latency <= 1.25x baseline (requires approval note to Sales/Leadership)

Deliverables by EOD Apr 15
- Per-model CSV (accuracy + latency)
- Failure-case samples (10-20 examples)
- Cost estimate for a production rollout (per 1M tokens inferred)

Marissa/Aditya — anything to add or pushback on timeline?

Thanks,
Lauren
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: PayGrid eval kickoff + parity acceptance planning (PG-3421)

Sounds good — I'll start the runs tomorrow morning. Notes: 

- Model selection: I recommend prioritizing open-7b-llama-compat (quantized at 8-bit first) and open-2.7b-quant; run the NeoX candidate as a fallback. Open-7b has historically matched rwx-3b-prop on entity extraction when we tune prompts.
- Quantization profiles: Jonas and I will try 8-bit then 4-bit-with-aware-calibration only if 8-bit misses cost targets.
- Benchmarks / references: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/paygrid-vs-open-2027 — we'll reuse the eval harness there for consistency.

On acceptance thresholds: I agree with the two-tier approach (strict vs soft). I'll capture both in the summary and flag if any open candidate clears strict.

Deliverables timeline:
- Apr 13 AM: initial run results (sample of 2k prompts)
- Apr 14 EOD: full 7-day run artifacts + failure-case doc

I'll upload intermediate CSV `eval_results_baseline_vs_open.csv` to the Drive folder and link it in the final memo.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@paygrid.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@paygrid.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Sandbox credentials + schedule for PayGrid eval (PG-3421)

Hi Sarah / Tom — looping you in with the provisioning details. We've reserved the sandbox and scheduled the first wave of eval runs tomorrow morning.

What you'll get:
- S3 upload link (expires in 7 days): https://s3.redwood.internal/paygrid-sandbox-upload/PG-3421 (I'll DM credentials)
- Initial run: open-7b-llama-compat (8-bit), open-2.7b-quant, rwx-3b-prop; run on a 24-hr cadence for the 7-day test.
- Cost estimate (approx): 45–60 GPU hours total for the initial 7-day grid (NVIDIA A10G equiv). I'll attach a short cost breakdown to the Drive folder.

Next steps for PayGrid:
- Please upload the anonymized sample CSV to the S3 link or the Drive folder.
- Confirm if you want us to prioritize extra focus on multi-entity grouping failure cases.

Attaching: redwood_model_recommendations.pdf (short deck with config notes).

Thanks — will update with the initial 2k prompt sample results ASAP.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
